subject.title: fix: sleep tool — session-targeted wake, correct sandbox policy, doc fixes

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` tool, and if so should it be implemented as an agent-scoped cron wrapper or a dedicated Gateway resume primitive?
rationale: The PR adds a new model-facing core scheduling capability and crosses session-state, cron, and sandbox-policy boundaries, so automation can identify defects but cannot choose the permanent product/API semantics.

options.title: Sponsor corrected core sleep
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require the PR or replacement to use the supported agent-scoped scheduling path, add catalog/profile coverage, and provide real same-session proof.

options.title: Keep cron as the scheduling surface
options.body: Reject a separate core sleep tool for now and keep delayed work on the existing cron and process-completion surfaces.

options.title: Define a plugin/API seam first
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers decide whether optional scheduling should live behind an extension seam rather than the default core tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor corrected core sleep
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction but require the PR or replacement to use the supported agent-scoped scheduling path, add catalog/profile coverage, and provide real same-session proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent tool registry/catalog and cron session-target history make this the strongest available owner for the product/API decision.
